extracted.intended_audience: Shakespeare scholars, students, editors, and general readers of the First Folio/annotated editions
extracted.subtask_description: Bibliographic and editorial material from a scholarly edition of Shakespeare, including biographical documents, First Folio prefatory matter, eulogies, extracts from contemporary sources, and an index to characters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Index inclusion and recording convention
rubrics_metrics.description: This Index records the act and scene in which each character first speaks, not necessarily the same as that in which he first appears. Only persons who speak are included, except a few marked with asterisk.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Record for each character the act and scene of first SPEECH (not first appearance); exclude silent characters except where explicitly marked with an asterisk.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editorial transcription conventions (erased/interlined material)
rubrics_metrics.description: [10] The words which have been erased are put between brackets; those which have been interlined are printed in italics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When presenting manuscript variants/transcription: show erased words in square brackets and interlined (inserted) words in italics so readers can distinguish deletions and insertions in the source.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editorial aim to restore authoritative texts (First Folio principle)
rubrics_metrics.description: …those (before) you were abus'd with diverse stolne and surreptitious copies, maimed and deformed by the frauds and stealthes of injurious impostors that expos'd them; even those are now offer'd to your view cur'd and perfect of their limbes, and all the rest absolute in their numbers as he conceived them;
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aim to produce a corrected, authoritative edition by repairing 'stolen' or corrupt texts and presenting the plays 'cured and perfect' and 'absolute in their numbers as [the author] conceived them' — i.e., prefer texts that reflect the author's intended form over surreptitious or corrupted copies.
